findings.title: Materials' 66-point lens gap signals earnings collapse
findings.body: Materials trades at 15.96x forward but 34.18x trailing, a 66-point percentile gap between the two lenses. The market is underwriting 114 percent earnings growth, which would be the rare case where a sector's forward multiple looks cheap only because analysts expect a dramatic profit recovery.

findings.title: Health Care's one-month re-rating is extreme
findings.body: Health Care's forward percentile jumped 24 points in a month to 96, yet its trailing percentile sits at 80. That 45 percent multiple compression implies analysts expect 83 percent earnings growth, a bet that the sector's current profitability is far below what it will deliver.

findings.title: Consumer Staples' week-long surge defies its range
findings.body: Consumer Staples' forward percentile rose 34 points in a single week to 42, while its trailing percentile is 76. The forward multiple at 19.83x is still below the trailing 27.44x, so the market is pricing in 38 percent earnings growth that has yet to appear in reported results.
